subject.title: [Security] Missing complexity validation and rate limiting on log query filters

question: Does any supported or internal historical-log, audit-ledger, task-ledger, or ACP method accept attacker-controlled recursive filter expressions that reach SQLite query construction?
rationale: The named files do not expose the alleged path, but only an owner-level audit can safely determine whether the report identified the wrong ingress or whether no vulnerable boundary exists.

options.title: Confirm the actual ingress
options.body: Request the exact method, request payload, authentication level, and generated query path, then implement bounded typed filters at that owner boundary if reproduced.

options.title: Close after full boundary audit
options.body: Close as unsubstantiated only after confirming that all related history and ledger methods accept fixed scalar filters with bounded limits.

options.title: Add broad defensive controls
options.body: Introduce shared query budgets or principal-scoped throttling only if maintainers intentionally want defense in depth across multiple ledger surfaces.

recommendation.title: Confirm the actual ingress
recommendation.body: Request the exact method, request payload, authentication level, and generated query path, then implement bounded typed filters at that owner boundary if reproduced.

likelyOwner.reason: The issue timeline identifies this person as a routing candidate for the ACP/security boundary, though direct history ownership remains uncertain.
